about: The list of Wazza skills. One source for the README, the Skills page in the app and agents. A shipped entry has a folder skills/<id>/ with a SKILL.md; scripts/check.py keeps the two in step.

skills.title: Measure a render before you post it
skills.line: Loudness, flashing, colour levels and file specs, with a fix for each failure.
skills.summary: Your agent cannot watch video; it looks at stills. This skill measures the whole render against delivery rules and hands the agent one finding per rule with its fix, so it can repair the render and check again.
steps: Sends the render to the delivery check, with the deep pass for flashing and banding
Reads each failed rule and its fix
Fixes the source, renders again and checks again, up to three rounds
skills.note: Loudness is judged against a delivery profile: Netflix, Prime Video, Apple, EBU, ATSC or review. A pass is a measurement, not a safety or compliance certificate.

skills.title: Long video to vertical shorts
skills.line: Your agent picks the moments; Wazza crops them to 9:16 and burns in captions.
skills.summary: For a podcast, a stream or any long clip. Your agent reads the transcript and picks the moments worth posting. Wazza cuts each one, crops it to 9:16 and burns in its captions.
steps: Transcribes the clip, up to 30 minutes
Picks up to 20 segments, each up to 120 seconds, and shows you the list
Runs the shorts workflow: one captioned vertical short per segment
skills.note: A segment that fails does not fail the others.

skills.title: Make generated shots look less generated
skills.line: A critique of all your shots, then the fix it proposes, applied to each shot that needs one.
skills.summary: For shots made with video models. Your agent sends one to six shots. Wazza reads them together, proposes a fix for whatever gives each one away, and applies it.
steps: Sends 1 to 6 shots of a scene to the unslop workflow
Reads what the critique found in each shot
Gets back each shot that needed a fix, with the fix applied
skills.note: A shot with nothing to fix is left as it is. It changes the look, not motion or anatomy errors.

skills.title: Sound for a silent render
skills.line: Foley written to the picture, plus effects and music your agent places.
skills.summary: Video rendered from code comes out silent. Wazza watches the clip and writes foley for it. Effects and a music track come back as separate files, and your agent places and mixes them with ffmpeg.
steps: Gets foley for the clip: the clip with sound, and the sound alone
Generates each effect the timeline calls for
Generates a music track and mixes everything with ffmpeg
skills.note: Music made for general use is for social and the web. A film, a TV programme or a game needs music made for picture.

skills.title: Dub a video into another language
skills.line: One run per language, clips up to 10 minutes. The voice changes, the lips do not.
skills.summary: Give your agent a finished video and the languages you want. It runs one dub per language, adds subtitles, and checks each version.
steps: Dubs the clip into each language, one run each
Adds subtitles: sidecar files in up to 5 languages per run, or burned in
Checks each version with wazza-check
skills.note: The speech is replaced; mouths are not re-animated.

skills.title: Generate video and images, price first
skills.line: Your agent picks the model for the shot, quotes the run, then makes it.
skills.summary: Many video and image models through one connection. Your agent picks the model from what the shot needs: a draft or a final, the resolution, the length, sound, a start frame or references. It quotes each run before it starts.
steps: Reads the models and what each one takes
Prices the run and tells you before it starts
Runs it, waits for the file and hands it back
skills.note: The model list and its prices change; your agent reads them live each time.

skills.title: From a script to boards and an animatic
skills.line: A shot list, boards with the same characters, temp voices, and an animatic cut with ffmpeg.
skills.summary: Give your agent a script or a brief. It writes the shot list, makes reference views of the cast, draws one board per shot, reads the dialogue in temp voices and cuts an animatic. It can lay out a deck from the boards.
steps: Writes the shot list and shows it to you
Makes character and set views, then one board per shot
Reads the dialogue, adds temp music and cuts the animatic with ffmpeg
skills.note: Wazza has no storyboard tool: your agent joins the image, orbit and voice tools, and makes the animatic and the deck itself.

skills.title: Masters that pass delivery QC
skills.line: Measure first, then conform to ProRes, DNxHR, 16-bit PNG or EXR, then check the master.
skills.summary: For a film, an episode or a shot that must go to a platform or a vendor. Your agent measures the source, fixes what the conform cannot, conforms it to the codec and raster of the spec, and checks the delivered file.
steps: Measures the source with the deep delivery check
Conforms it, with an upscale when the raster needs one
Checks the master and each audio file against the profile
skills.note: Wazza does not mix or build audio stems; it measures them. A pass is a measurement, not the distributor's QC.

skills.title: Narration and voices
skills.line: Reads a script or a whole scene in the workspace's voices, or designs a new voice.
skills.summary: Your agent lists the voices of your workspace, then reads a script in one of them, a scene in several voices as one take, or a recording again in another voice. It can also design three previews of a new voice from a description.
steps: Lists the voices and lets you pick
Prices and reads the script or the scene
Hands back the audio, with line timings for a scene
skills.note: A cloned voice is a real person's: your agent asks before it uses one. A designed voice is saved in the app.

skills.title: From an image to a 3D model
skills.line: A textured GLB from a picture or several views, cleaned for Blender, Unity, Unreal or Godot.
skills.summary: Give your agent a picture of a prop or a character. Wazza makes a textured model, and can rebuild its topology, unwrap its UVs or split it into parts. Your agent brings it into the engine.
steps: Cuts the subject out and makes more views if needed
Makes the textured model in the profile the use calls for
Cleans topology and UVs, then imports it into the engine
skills.note: A model from one picture guesses the sides it cannot see; several views give more control.

skills.title: Check a VFX return against its pull
Solve the grade between two shots
